formats.key: stake(uint128 amount, uint64 end)
effects: Takes `amount` STONX from the signer by transferFrom to the Ekubo Core accountant (payFrom), spending the signer's STONX allowance to VeToken.
Mints a new veSTONX NFT with a random ID to the signer. The NFT controls the stake.
Locks the STONX in Ve33 until timestamp `end`.
Any native value sent is not used, because the stake token is an ERC20. It stays in the contract, and anyone can take it with refundNativeToken.
formats.shown: Says 'Stake {amount} STONX', with the amount and the stake end date.

findings.title: stake is payable but no @.value field is shown, and native value sent is left in the contract.
findings.evidence: VeToken.sol stake(uint128,uint64) is `public payable`. stakeToken is the ERC20 0x570C…70C5, so handleLockData never uses msg.value. receive() is payable, and PayableMulticallable.refundNativeToken() sends address(this).balance to any caller. The descriptor format has only amount and end.
findings.fix: Add a field {path:'@.value', label:'Native value', format:'amount'}, or state that the value must be 0.

findings.title: stake: the minted NFT ID is random, so it is not shown.
findings.evidence: stake(uint128,uint64) calls stake(amount,end,_randomSalt()). The ID comes from prevrandao and gas.
findings.fix: None needed. The intent 'Create vote-escrow stake' already implies a new position.

formats.key: burn(uint256 veId)
effects: Burns the veSTONX NFT veId and clears its stored end date, without checking that the stake is empty.
If the stake still holds STONX or fees, they become permanently unreachable, because stakeId(veId) reverts with TokenDoesNotExist after the burn.
Any native value sent is not used and is left claimable by anyone.
formats.shown: Says 'Burn empty vote-escrow NFT', with the stake ID.

findings.title: burn says the NFT is 'empty', but the code burns any NFT and any remaining stake is lost for good.
findings.evidence: VeToken.sol burn(): `_burn(veId); _setExtraData(veId, 0);` has no check on ve33.stakeAmount. _stakeEndTime reverts TokenDoesNotExist afterwards, so withdrawStake can never reach the stake. The descriptor intent is 'Burn empty vote-escrow NFT'.
findings.fix: Use the intent 'Burn stake NFT {veId}: any STONX or fees still in it are lost forever'.

findings.format: burn(uint256 veId)
findings.title: burn says the NFT is 'empty', but the code burns any NFT and any remaining stake is lost for good.
findings.reason: The function burns an authorized NFT without checking that its stake is empty, removing access to any remaining stake through normal withdrawal. The misleading 'empty' assurance is proven, although permanent irrecoverability under every possible remint scenario is not established.
findings.quote: VeToken.sol, burn: '_burn(veId); _setExtraData(veId, 0);'; _stakeEndTime: 'if (!_exists(veId)) revert TokenDoesNotExist();'; withdrawStake: 'StakeId id = stakeId(veId);'. descriptor.json, burn: 'intent': 'Burn empty vote-escrow NFT', field 'veId'.

findings.format: burn(uint256 veId)
findings.title: burn is payable but no @.value field is shown.
findings.reason: The payable burn changes NFT storage without consuming or refunding attached native value. The screen shows no native transfer.
findings.quote: VeToken.sol, burn: 'function burn(uint256 veId) external payable authorizedForStake(veId) { _burn(veId); _setExtraData(veId, 0); }'. descriptor.json: 'Burn empty vote-escrow NFT', field 'veId'.

findings.format: vote(uint256 veId, (address token0, address token1, bytes32 config) poolKey, uint64 swapFee)
findings.title: vote is payable but no @.value field is shown.
findings.reason: The vote call forwards no native value to Ve33 and performs no refund. Successful execution retains the undisclosed attached amount.
findings.quote: VeToken.sol, vote: 'public payable authorizedForStake(veId)' and 've33.vote(stakeId(veId), poolKey, swapFee);'. descriptor.json: 'Vote for pool fee', fields 'veId', 'poolKey.token0', 'poolKey.token1', 'poolKey.config', 'swapFee'.

findings.format: clearVote(uint256 veId)
findings.title: clearVote discards unclaimed voter fees, and the screen does not say so.
findings.reason: The supplied code establishes the call to clearVote, but not how Ve33 handles accrued fees. The fee-discarding implementation and mined evidence are absent.
findings.quote: VeToken.sol, clearVote: 've33.clearVote(stakeId(veId));'; IVe33.sol: 'function clearVote(StakeId stakeId) external;'. VeToken.sol, claimPoolFeesAndExtendStake devdoc says 'pending fees are discarded when votes are cleared'; descriptor.json says 'Clear pool vote'.

findings.format: clearVote(uint256 veId)
findings.title: clearVote is payable but no @.value field is shown.
findings.reason: The payable clearVote wrapper calls Ve33 without forwarding native value. It retains the attached amount without displaying it.
findings.quote: VeToken.sol, clearVote: 'function clearVote(uint256 veId) external payable authorizedForStake(veId) { ve33.clearVote(stakeId(veId)); }'. descriptor.json: 'Clear pool vote', field 'veId'.

findings.format: claimPoolFees(uint256 veId, (address token0, address token1, bytes32 config) poolKey, address recipient)
findings.title: claimPoolFees is payable but no @.value field is shown.
findings.reason: The claim path pays accrued fees from the accountant, not from the attached transaction value. That attached value remains undisclosed in the wrapper.
findings.quote: VeToken.sol, claimPoolFees: 'public payable' and 'lock(abi.encode(CALL_TYPE_CLAIM_POOL_FEES, veId, recipient, poolKey))'; handleLockData: 'ACCOUNTANT.withdrawTwo(poolKey.token0, poolKey.token1, recipient, amount0, amount1);'. descriptor.json: 'Claim voter fees', fields 'veId', 'recipient', 'poolKey.token0', 'poolKey.token1', 'poolKey.config'.

findings.format: claimPoolFeesToSelf(uint256 veId, (address token0, address token1, bytes32 config) poolKey)
findings.title: claimPoolFeesToSelf is payable but no @.value field is shown.
findings.reason: Directing the claimed fees to the signer does not refund attached native value. Successful calls retain that separate amount without displaying it.
findings.quote: VeToken.sol, claimPoolFeesToSelf: 'public payable' and '(amount0, amount1) = claimPoolFees(veId, poolKey, msg.sender);'; handleLockData pays through 'ACCOUNTANT.withdrawTwo(...)'. descriptor.json: 'Claim voter fees', fields 'veId', 'poolKey.token0', 'poolKey.token1', 'poolKey.config'.

findings.format: maybeInitializePool((address token0, address token1, bytes32 config) poolKey, int32 tick)
findings.title: maybeInitializePool is payable but no @.value field is shown.
findings.reason: The payable initialization helper never uses attached native value, including the already-initialized success branch. Intended multicall use does not enforce a refund.
findings.quote: VeToken.sol, maybeInitializePool: 'external payable'; 'if (state.isInitialized()) { sqrtRatio = state.sqrtRatio(); } else { initialized = true; sqrtRatio = CORE.initializePool(poolKey, tick); }'. descriptor.json: 'Initialize Ve33 pool if needed', fields 'poolKey.token0', 'poolKey.token1', 'poolKey.config', 'tick'.

findings.format: multicall(bytes[] data)
findings.title: multicall is payable but no @.value field is shown.
findings.reason: The override bypasses the base multicall's nonzero-value rejection. An empty batch succeeds and retains all attached native value, while the screen shows only actions.
findings.quote: PayableMulticallable.sol, multicall: 'function multicall(bytes[] calldata data) public payable override returns (bytes[] memory) { _multicallDirectReturn(_multicall(data)); }'; Multicallable.sol, _multicall: 'if data.length { ... }'. descriptor.json: 'Batch vote-escrow actions', field 'data.[]' labeled 'Action'.

findings.format: approve(address account, uint256 id)
findings.title: approve is payable but no @.value field is shown.
findings.reason: The inherited payable approval updates authorization without spending or refunding native value. The descriptor shows only the approval account and NFT ID.
findings.quote: lib/solady/src/tokens/ERC721.sol, approve: 'function approve(address account, uint256 id) public payable virtual { _approve(msg.sender, account, id); }'. descriptor.json: 'Approve Stake NFT', fields 'account', 'id'.

findings.format: transferFrom(address from, address to, uint256 id)
findings.title: transferFrom is payable but no @.value field is shown.
findings.reason: The inherited payable transfer changes NFT ownership but leaves attached native value in VeToken. No screen field states that separate transfer.
findings.quote: lib/solady/src/tokens/ERC721.sol, transferFrom: 'function transferFrom(address from, address to, uint256 id) public payable virtual' and 'sstore(ownershipSlot, xor(ownershipPacked, xor(from, to)))'; transfer hooks are empty. descriptor.json: 'Transfer Stake NFT', fields 'from', 'to', 'id'.

findings.format: safeTransferFrom(address from, address to, uint256 id)
findings.title: safeTransferFrom is payable but no @.value field is shown.
findings.reason: A safe transfer to an EOA completes through transferFrom and retains attached native value. The screen displays only the NFT transfer.
findings.quote: lib/solady/src/tokens/ERC721.sol, safeTransferFrom(address,address,uint256): 'public payable virtual', 'transferFrom(from, to, id);', 'if (_hasCode(to)) _checkOnERC721Received(from, to, id, "");'. descriptor.json: 'Transfer Stake NFT', fields 'from', 'to', 'id'.

findings.format: safeTransferFrom(address from, address to, uint256 id, bytes data)
findings.title: safeTransferFrom with data is payable but no @.value field is shown.
findings.reason: The data overload likewise retains attached native value on successful transfers, including transfers to EOAs. Showing callback data does not disclose that amount.
findings.quote: lib/solady/src/tokens/ERC721.sol, safeTransferFrom(address,address,uint256,bytes): 'public payable virtual', 'transferFrom(from, to, id);', 'if (_hasCode(to)) _checkOnERC721Received(from, to, id, data);'. descriptor.json: 'Transfer Stake NFT', fields 'from', 'to', 'id', 'data'.

findings.format: refundNativeToken()
findings.title: refundNativeToken is payable, and no field shows the ETH sent (@.value)
findings.reason: Successful execution returns the entire native balance, including attached value, to the caller. The screen states a native-token refund and shows the caller as recipient; the severity guide explicitly exempts funds returned to the caller.
findings.quote: PayableMulticallable.sol, refundNativeToken: 'SafeTransferLib.safeTransferETH(msg.sender, address(this).balance);'. descriptor.json: 'Refund unused native token', field '@.from' labeled 'Recipient'. Severity guide <not_critical> 4: 'funds that return to the caller. Not a different recipient; not a finding, or a warning when a field would help.'
